Some publication present the DMRs as signal to noise ratio (mean methylation on test samples - mean methylation on control samples : sd of test samples + sd of control samples). Is there anywhere I can look for these informations on methylKit objects? I assume I can take meth.diff value as mean methylation on test samples - mean methylation on control samples, but I did not see how to find the standard deviations.

Thanks in advance,
Milan

messages.subject_clean: plotting DMR at chromosomal scale
messages.body_plain:
I think on chromosomal scale everything will look a bit squished and uninformative if you don't have strong genome/chromsome wide signals. But if you want to get the sd of groups and do a  plot based on that, you can do that. Also default options is that the differences between means of groups are differences between weighted means, weights are coverages.

Anyway, you can get the sds and means as follows
methMat=percMethylation(methylBase.obj)# methMat has the same row order as methylBase.obj
library(matrixStats)
# means and sds for the first group
mean0=rowMeans(methMat[, methylBase.obj@treament==0])
sd0=rowSds(methMat[, methylBase.obj@treament==0])

# means and sds the second group of samples
mean1=rowMeans(methMat[, methylBase.obj@treament==1])
sd1=rowSds(methMat[, methylBase.obj@treament==1])

messages.body_plain:
This could be a bit more complicated than just using the tilling function since every gene  has different length, and if you want to overlay the genes on top of each other and get an average profile change you need to bin the genes differently. If that's what you want to do, I think the genes should be binned to equal number of bins depending on their total length. So the bin length could be 10% of the total length. So that each gene will have 10 bins, and you can more or less compare them to each other. This won't nicely work if the gene lengths are too different, maybe do this for genes that are not too short or too long.

But this can not be done in methylKit but we have another package called genomation (https://github.com/al2na/genomation) that can do this. You can use the ScoreMatrixBin() function to achieve that. You can ask your questions about genomation at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/genomation if you have problems using it.

Best,
Altuna

There is no function to do that but you can use the following code piece. But I use it with caution, you need to change two things in the methylRawList object.

data(methylKit)

#assume myNewMethylRaw is a new methylRaw object
myNewMethylRaw=methylRawList.obj[[1]]

# 1) add a new methylRaw object to methylRawList
methylRawList.obj[[length(methylRawList.obj)+1]]=myNewMethylRaw

# 2) update the treatment vector in the methylRawList object
#    the treatment vector designates the sample groups
methylRawList.obj@treatment=c(methylRawList.obj@treatment,0)

 I might convert this to a function later on to make sure users do not violate the object structure when adding new objects to the methylRawList and cause problems in the downstream analysis.
